title: signal 4 on freebsd arm64 due to missing cache synchronisation
body: I run Firefox newer than 115 on FreeBSD arm64. With write-protected code disabled for content processes, JIT code kills Firefox with signal 4. FreeBSD needs to execute the cache-synchronization code in MozCpu-vixl.cpp so that newly written JIT code is ready to execute.

symptoms_visible: On FreeBSD arm64, running JIT code in Firefox newer than 115 kills Firefox with signal 4 when content-process code pages remain writable and executable.
N0.label: N0 FreeBSD arm64 JIT crash reported

symptoms_visible: Firefox still exits with signal 4 when JIT code executes on the affected FreeBSD arm64 configuration.
N1.label: N1 unrelated ASLR issue separated

symptoms_visible: Firefox still exits with signal 4 when JIT code executes on the affected FreeBSD arm64 configuration.
N2.label: N2 cache-invalidation diagnosis established

symptoms_visible: I was able to build and test my candidate source patch with Firefox 122 build2 on FreeBSD.
N3.label: N3 candidate patch authored and tested

symptoms_visible: The revised candidate patch is ready for upstream integration; I have not reported testing an upstream build containing the landed change.
N4.label: N4 final patch revision ready

symptoms_visible: The FreeBSD instruction-cache invalidation patch has landed upstream, but I have not reported retesting the original JIT workload on an upstream build containing it.
N_terminal.label: terminal patch landed without reporter retest

question_patterns: Is the separate MAP_FIXED change required to solve this signal 4 failure, or is it a different problem?
Can you separate the JIT crash from the other FreeBSD memory-mapping issue?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: The MAP_FIXED change solves running with ASLR on FreeBSD and is another story that I still have to investigate. It is unrelated to the JIT crash with signal 4.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The signal 4 failure still occurs after cache synchronization and only stops when the MAP_FIXED change is applied.
I would prefer to discuss the ASLR work in a separate bug.

edges.comment: Comments 3 and 6, concerning the opening reporter's FreeBSD arm64 system. A maintainer questioned whether MAP_FIXED belonged in this fix, and the reporter explicitly separated that ASLR problem from the signal 4 JIT crash.

solution.intent: Diagnose the FreeBSD arm64 crash as stale JIT instructions caused by missing instruction-cache invalidation after the move away from mprotect transitions, while keeping the separate MAP_FIXED/ASLR work out of this fix.
solution.concrete_example: On arm64, newly written JIT instructions require explicit instruction-cache invalidation. The earlier mprotect transition had masked FreeBSD's missing cache-synchronization path; the MAP_FIXED work addresses a separate ASLR problem.
solution.inference_hint: The reporter supplied the missing-cache-synchronization diagnosis and identified the FreeBSD exclusion. Maintainers connected it to stale ARM instruction-cache contents, explained why mprotect had hidden it, and traced the native-aarch64 fallthrough to the earlier OpenBSD portability change.

edges.comment: Comments 3, 6 and 7: maintainers accept the reporter's cache diagnosis, explain the stale-instruction mechanism and mprotect masking, and identify the earlier OpenBSD fix as the likely regression source.

question_patterns: Would you like to author the upstream patch, or should a maintainer prepare it?
Can you prepare and attach the source change for review?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I would like to be the author. I should be able to attach a patch tomorrow.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: Please have a maintainer prepare the equivalent patch instead.

solution.intent: Implement the FreeBSD arm64 instruction-cache invalidation path and prevent unsupported native arm64 platforms from silently entering the non-arm64 simulator fallback.
solution.concrete_example: Extend the native arm64 cache-maintenance branch to FreeBSD and add an explicit native-aarch64 guard so an unhandled operating system cannot reach the block documented as being only for a non-aarch64 simulator.

edges.comment: Comments 6 and 8-12, all concerning the opening reporter's patch. After agreeing to author it, the reporter attached a patch against tip, volunteered that testing was limited to Firefox 122 build2, and explained the tentative OpenBSD exception. Preparing and retaining the source change creates persistent state S1b.

solution.intent: Revise the candidate patch after review so the related CPU cache-type guards are handled consistently without retaining an inappropriate compile-time error in GetCacheType.
solution.concrete_example: Apply the same platform-guard strategy to CPU::GetCacheType, then revise that portion so GetCacheType itself does not error out, producing the final patch revision.
solution.inference_hint: The final implementation history consists of the reporter's successive cacheinvalidation2 and cacheinvalidation3 attachments. The Try source retained the reporter's authorship even though the review interface displayed the submitter.

edges.comment: Comments 13-18: the same reporter's source patch moves through review and is revised twice. The retained final revision is persistent state S1c. Authorship-display logistics are not scored.

solution.intent: Land the reviewed FreeBSD instruction-cache invalidation patch, then ask the affected reporter to retest a build containing it before declaring the runtime failure resolved.
solution.concrete_example: Integrate the reviewed change that uses instruction-cache invalidation on FreeBSD arm64. After it is available in a current build, ask the reporter to run the original JIT workload again and report whether signal 4 is gone.
solution.inference_hint: The thread records that the reviewed FreeBSD cache-invalidation change landed upstream and was also integrated into beta. It does not contain a subsequent message from the affected reporter confirming the original workload on a landed build.

edges.comment: Comments 19-27: maintainers and bots report the patch landing upstream and in beta. These are engineering and release records, not an affected-user verification. The graph therefore ends with a landed but reporter-unverified state.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the accepted root cause: native FreeBSD arm64 was omitted from the JIT instruction-cache invalidation path, so after content-process JIT pages changed to remain writable and executable, stale instructions could be executed and Firefox exited with signal 4.
Must ground the diagnosis in the reported FreeBSD arm64 behavior, the change away from mprotect transitions, and the candidate patch test rather than treating signal 4 as a generic crash.
Must recommend the upstream technical fix: execute the native arm64 instruction-cache synchronization path on FreeBSD and avoid silently treating an unhandled native-aarch64 host as a simulator.
Must not fold the separate FreeBSD MAP_FIXED/ASLR work into the signal 4 fix; the reporter explicitly identified it as another issue.
Must ask the affected reporter to retest a build containing the landed fix and must not claim user-verified resolution, because the thread ends after landing without such a retest.

persona_hint.experience_level: Highly technical FreeBSD contributor familiar with arm64 JIT behavior, memory-protection policy, Mozilla source code, local ports patches, and building Firefox from source.
persona_hint.communication_style: Direct and implementation-focused; supplies source locations and patches, distinguishes unrelated platform issues, responds carefully to review questions, and states testing limitations plainly.
